options.a: Pneumonia, as if the diagnosis were confirmed
options.b: An observation Z code for suspected pneumonia
options.c: The documented signs and symptoms (cough, fever)
options.d: R69, illness, unspecified, until the test results return

distractorExplanations.d: R69 is a nonspecific unspecified-illness code; the documented cough and fever are more specific and are coded instead.
distractorExplanations.a: Coding an uncertain diagnosis as confirmed is the inpatient rule, not the outpatient rule.
distractorExplanations.b: Z03 observation codes are for a suspected condition that is ruled out with no signs or symptoms present.

options.a: Makes notes too short to support the level of service billed
options.b: Forces coders to assign unspecified diagnosis codes
options.c: Is prohibited in every EHR by federal software rules
options.d: May carry forward findings or services that did not occur

distractorExplanations.a: Cloned notes tend to be long and repetitive; the compliance risk is inaccurate carried-forward content, not brevity.
distractorExplanations.b: Cloning does not force unspecified codes; it undermines the integrity of the record.
distractorExplanations.c: Copy-paste is not banned outright; it must be used responsibly and audited.

options.a: The patient's ASA physical status classification
options.b: The anesthesia provider's level of supervision
options.c: The emergency status of the surgical procedure
options.d: The base unit value of the anesthesia code

distractorExplanations.b: Supervision level is shown with modifiers such as AA, QK, QX, and QZ.
distractorExplanations.c: Emergency conditions are reported with qualifying circumstance code 99140.
distractorExplanations.d: Base units come from the anesthesia code itself, not the P modifier.

options.a: To verify that staff completed annual HIPAA training
options.b: To confirm that each provider holds a valid, active NPI number
options.c: To avoid billing federal programs for excluded parties
options.d: To check that coders passed a credentialing exam

distractorExplanations.b: NPI status is checked in NPPES; an active NPI says nothing about whether the person is excluded by the OIG.
distractorExplanations.a: Training records are tracked separately from exclusion screening.
distractorExplanations.d: Exam credentialing is verified with AHIMA or AAPC, not the LEIE.

options.c: B
options.d: X

distractorExplanations.b: 1 is the Obstetrics section.
distractorExplanations.c: B is the Imaging section.
distractorExplanations.d: X is the New Technology section.

options.a: Body part
options.b: Surgical approach
options.c: Root operation
options.d: Body system

distractorExplanations.b: The approach (how the operative site is reached) is the 5th character, not the 3rd character of the code.
distractorExplanations.d: The body system is the 2nd character; the 3rd character identifies the root operation (objective of the procedure).
distractorExplanations.a: Body part is the 4th character.

options.a: Extirpation
options.b: Destruction
options.c: Shock Wave Therapy
options.d: Fragmentation

distractorExplanations.c: Shock Wave Therapy is a root operation in the Extracorporeal or Systemic Therapies section for musculoskeletal treatment; breaking up a stone is Fragmentation.
distractorExplanations.a: Extirpation requires the solid matter to be taken out.
distractorExplanations.b: Destruction eradicates a body part itself, not solid matter within it.

options.a: Supplement
options.b: Reposition
options.c: Replacement
options.d: Insertion

distractorExplanations.a: Supplement reinforces a body part that remains in place.
distractorExplanations.b: Reposition moves a body part to its normal location.
distractorExplanations.d: Insertion places a nonbiological device that does not replace a body part.

options.b: X
options.c: Y
options.d: Z

distractorExplanations.a: 0 is a specific value in many tables, not "no device."
distractorExplanations.b: X as a 7th-character qualifier means Diagnostic.
distractorExplanations.c: Y is used for "other device" in some tables, not for no device.

options.a: The two conditions are never coded together
options.b: The excluded condition may be coded additionally if present
options.c: The excluded code must always be sequenced first
options.d: The code requires an additional 7th character

distractorExplanations.b: "May also be coded if present" describes Excludes2.
distractorExplanations.c: Sequencing instructions come from "code first" and "use additional code" notes.
distractorExplanations.d: 7th-character requirements are separate tabular instructions.

aapc-ccs-readiness-check-icd-001.explanation: Excludes1 is a pure exclusion: the two codes cannot be reported together because the conditions cannot occur together, such as congenital and acquired forms of the same condition. Guidelines allow limited exceptions when the conditions are unrelated. The conditions are mutually exclusive.

options.a: The two conditions cannot be reported on the same claim
options.b: The excluded condition is reported as a manifestation code after it
options.c: Both codes may be reported if both conditions are present
options.d: The code is valid only for inpatient encounters

distractorExplanations.a: Not reporting the two conditions together describes Excludes1 (pure exclusion), not Excludes2.
distractorExplanations.b: Excludes2 is unrelated to the etiology/manifestation convention; that sequencing comes from code first/use additional code notes.
distractorExplanations.d: Excludes notes apply in every setting.

options.a: Add the placeholder "X" to fill the empty positions
options.b: Report the code without adding the 7th character
options.c: Add zeros in the empty positions before the 7th character
options.d: Assign the 7th character in the next open position

distractorExplanations.c: Zero is a meaningful code character, not a placeholder; ICD-10-CM uses the letter X to fill empty positions.
distractorExplanations.d: The 7th character must sit in position 7; placing it in the 5th or 6th position creates an invalid or different code.
distractorExplanations.b: Omitting a required 7th character makes the code invalid.

options.a: Sequenced first as the principal diagnosis
options.b: Sequenced after the code for the underlying etiology
options.c: Reported alone, without the underlying condition
options.d: Sequenced first on outpatient claims, second on inpatient claims

distractorExplanations.d: The etiology/manifestation convention applies in every setting; these codes are never first-listed on outpatient claims either.
distractorExplanations.a: These manifestation codes may never be principal or first-listed.
distractorExplanations.c: The etiology code must always be reported with the manifestation.

options.a: Systemic infection code (e.g., A41.9) first, then N39.0
options.b: UTI (N39.0) first as the reason for admission, then A41.9
options.c: R65.20 severe sepsis first, then the organism
options.d: Either may be principal at the coder's discretion

distractorExplanations.b: When sepsis and a localized infection are both POA, the systemic infection is principal and the localized infection is secondary.
distractorExplanations.c: R65.2- codes cannot be sequenced first.
distractorExplanations.d: Guidelines give explicit sequencing for sepsis with a localized infection.

options.a: Other specified; no separate code exists for the detail
options.b: Not otherwise specified; the documentation lacks detail
options.c: Not on schedule; the code is new this fiscal year
options.d: Non-operative status; no procedure was performed

distractorExplanations.a: That definition describes NEC (other specified).
distractorExplanations.c: NOS has nothing to do with code update schedules.
distractorExplanations.d: NOS does not describe procedure status.

options.a: That was most expensive to treat during the stay
options.b: Listed first in the emergency department's records on arrival
options.c: Found after study to be chiefly responsible for admission
options.d: With the highest relative weight among all diagnoses

distractorExplanations.b: The ED working diagnosis at arrival may change after study; UHDDS uses the condition established after study.
distractorExplanations.a: Cost does not determine the principal diagnosis.
distractorExplanations.d: Choosing by DRG weight rather than the definition is noncompliant.

options.a: Not coded separately; they are routine for appendicitis
options.b: Coded first as the reason for the visit, then the appendicitis
options.c: Coded only when they appear on the discharge summary
options.d: Coded as secondary diagnoses to support severity

distractorExplanations.b: Symptoms integral to a confirmed diagnosis are not coded at all, so they cannot be sequenced ahead of the appendicitis.
distractorExplanations.c: Where they are documented does not matter; integral symptoms are not coded.
distractorExplanations.d: Coding integral symptoms adds redundant codes and is not allowed.

options.a: It must be billed with every related surgery
options.b: It is not reported when integral to a larger service
options.c: It is paid in addition to the main procedure at full value
options.d: It is reportable only with modifier 51 attached

distractorExplanations.c: When a separate procedure is integral to a larger service it is bundled, not paid in addition at full value.
distractorExplanations.a: A separate procedure is not billed with related surgery when it is integral to it.
distractorExplanations.d: Modifier 51 marks multiple procedures; it does not make a separate procedure reportable.

options.a: The suture material and needle type used
options.b: The anesthetic used and the time spent on the repair
options.c: Repair complexity, total length, and location
options.d: The total number of sutures that were placed

distractorExplanations.b: Local anesthesia is included in the repair code, and time spent is not a CPT repair criterion; length and complexity are.
distractorExplanations.a: Suture material does not change the repair code.
distractorExplanations.d: Suture count is not a CPT criterion; length and complexity are.

options.a: Report a separate code for each distinct body-part value
options.b: Report one code for the most significant site only
options.c: Report the code once and note the extra sites in the 7th character
options.d: Append a modifier to the code to show the multiple sites

distractorExplanations.c: The 7th character is the qualifier; it does not capture additional sites, so each distinct body-part value needs its own code.
distractorExplanations.d: ICD-10-PCS has no modifiers; site modifiers such as XS belong to CPT/HCPCS outpatient coding.
distractorExplanations.b: Coding one site under-reports distinct procedures.

options.a: Only the laparoscopic (percutaneous endoscopic) procedure
options.b: The open procedure plus a percutaneous endoscopic Inspection
options.c: The open procedure, with the conversion noted by a qualifier
options.d: Both the full laparoscopic and full open procedures

distractorExplanations.c: No qualifier captures a conversion; guideline B3.2d requires a separate percutaneous endoscopic Inspection code.
distractorExplanations.a: The procedure was completed open, so coding only the laparoscopic approach is wrong.
distractorExplanations.d: The procedure was performed once; the laparoscopic part is an Inspection only.

options.a: Via Natural or Artificial Opening With Percutaneous Endoscopic Assistance
options.b: Via Natural or Artificial Opening Endoscopic
options.c: Via Natural or Artificial Opening
options.d: Percutaneous Endoscopic

distractorExplanations.a: Value F is for procedures through a natural opening assisted laparoscopically (e.g. LAVH), not a laparoscope through a skin puncture.
distractorExplanations.b: Value 8 is an endoscope passed through a natural or artificial opening (e.g. colonoscopy), not through a skin puncture.
distractorExplanations.c: That approach enters through a natural orifice, such as the mouth or urethra.

options.a: Diagnoses, symptoms, and reasons for encounters
options.b: Physician services and surgical procedures
options.c: Supplies, drugs, and durable medical equipment
options.d: Inpatient hospital procedures, devices, and approaches

distractorExplanations.d: Inpatient procedures, devices and approaches are coded with ICD-10-PCS, not the ICD-10-CM diagnosis classification.
distractorExplanations.b: Physician services and procedures are reported with CPT.
distractorExplanations.c: Supplies, drugs, and DME are reported with HCPCS Level II.

options.a: The service is covered under the patient's benefit plan
options.b: The service is needed to diagnose or treat the patient
options.c: The patient requested the service in writing
options.d: The service is the least expensive option available

distractorExplanations.a: Coverage is a benefit question; a covered service can still be denied when documentation does not show clinical need.
distractorExplanations.c: A patient request does not make a service medically necessary.
distractorExplanations.d: Necessity is about clinical need, not price.

options.a: Reporting a higher-level service than documented/supported
options.b: Reporting a lower level than documented to avoid an audit
options.c: Billing separate codes for components of a bundled service
options.d: Billing for a service that the provider did not perform

distractorExplanations.b: Reporting a lower level than documented is downcoding (undercoding), also noncompliant but the opposite of upcoding.
distractorExplanations.c: Billing components of a bundled service separately is unbundling, a different improper coding practice.
distractorExplanations.d: Billing for services not rendered is phantom billing, a separate fraud type from inflating the level of a real service.

options.a: Honest billing errors corrected in a timely way
options.b: Knowingly submitting false claims to the government
options.c: Disputes between patients and private insurers
options.d: Claims filed after the payer's timely filing limit has passed

distractorExplanations.d: Missing the timely filing limit leads to a denial, not False Claims Act liability, which requires a knowingly false claim.
distractorExplanations.a: Honest mistakes corrected promptly lack the knowing intent the Act requires.
distractorExplanations.c: Private insurance disputes are not federal false claims.

options.a: Workplace safety rules and sharps injury logs
options.b: Billing fraud and the penalties for submitting false claims
options.c: Use and disclosure of protected health information
options.d: Referral fees and kickback payments by providers

distractorExplanations.b: False claims penalties come from the False Claims Act and related fraud statutes, not the HIPAA Privacy Rule.
distractorExplanations.a: Workplace safety and sharps logs fall under OSHA.
distractorExplanations.d: Kickbacks are covered by the Anti-Kickback Statute.

options.a: Diagnoses and reasons for visits
options.b: Inpatient hospital procedures and devices
options.c: Physician office visits and surgeries
options.d: Drugs, supplies, DME, and some services

distractorExplanations.b: Inpatient procedures and devices are coded in ICD-10-PCS; HCPCS Level II covers drugs, supplies and DME.
distractorExplanations.a: Diagnoses are reported with ICD-10-CM.
distractorExplanations.c: Office visits and surgeries are CPT (HCPCS Level I) codes.

options.a: A patient's 11-character Medicare Beneficiary Identifier
options.b: A unique 10-digit number for health care providers
options.c: A code for where a service was performed
options.d: A payer-assigned number for each claim filed

distractorExplanations.a: The 11-character MBI identifies the Medicare patient; the NPI is a 10-digit number identifying the provider.
distractorExplanations.c: Where a service happened is the place-of-service code.
distractorExplanations.d: Payers assign claim numbers; the NPI identifies the provider.

options.a: Reporting a panel code when all tests were done
options.b: Assigning a higher E/M level than documented
options.c: Billing parts separately when one code covers all
options.d: Reporting one comprehensive code that covers the whole service

distractorExplanations.d: Reporting the comprehensive code is correct coding, the opposite of unbundling the components separately.
distractorExplanations.a: Using the panel code when every component test was done is correct coding.
distractorExplanations.b: Billing a higher level than documented is upcoding, not unbundling.

options.a: A bilateral procedure performed at the same operative session
options.b: A distinct service not normally reported together
options.c: An assistant surgeon's participation
options.d: A significant, separate E/M service that day

distractorExplanations.a: Bilateral procedures at the same session are reported with modifier 50, not the distinct-service modifier 59/X{EPSU}.
distractorExplanations.c: Assistant surgeons use modifier 80.
distractorExplanations.d: A significant, separately identifiable E/M service uses modifier 25.

options.a: Move the case into a higher-weighted MS-DRG as an MCC
options.b: Be reported only as a Z code for tracking
options.c: Be deleted from the claim before submission
options.d: Not count as a CC/MCC to raise MS-DRG payment

distractorExplanations.a: The HAC-POA policy does the opposite: a selected condition with POA = N cannot act as a CC/MCC to raise the MS-DRG.
distractorExplanations.b: The condition keeps its own diagnosis code; it is not replaced by a Z code.
distractorExplanations.c: The condition must still be coded and reported accurately.
